scale_004:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a draft set of expense categories and spending limits for our expense management platform (e.g., Ramp, Expensify, or whatever tool we use — ask me which one if you don't already know, plus my domain/company name and whether you have configured credentials for that platform).

Goal: Produce a complete, well-organized draft expense category/limit table that finance leadership can review and approve — not a final policy.

Steps:
1. Ask me for: our expense platform, industry/company size context, and any existing expense policy documents or category lists I can share.
2. Research standard expense category structures typical for companies of our type (e.g., Travel, Meals & Entertainment, Office Supplies, Software/SaaS, Client Entertainment, Professional Development, Equipment, Mileage, Lodging, Communications).
3. Draft a table with: category name, description, suggested per-transaction limit, suggested monthly/annual cap, receipt requirement threshold, and approval tier (e.g., manager, director, VP) — clearly marked as placeholder/suggested values pending finance sign-off.
4. If credentials allow, check the platform's current category configuration and note any gaps or overlaps versus your draft, but do NOT create, edit, or apply any categories, limits, or workflow changes in the live system.
5. Compile a short checklist of open questions finance leadership must answer (e.g., "Confirm per diem rate," "Confirm card vs. reimbursement threshold").

Done looks like: a clearly labeled draft table plus an open-questions checklist, ready for finance leadership to review, adjust, and approve.

Report back with: the draft category/limit table, the checklist of open questions, any gaps found versus the current platform setup, and then stop for human sign-off — do not enter, save, or apply any of these limits in the live platform.

scale_004:n2.prompt:
You are helping me configure per-employee corporate card limits in {{vendor}}, our startup banking/card platform, as part of our expense management setup. 

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our {{vendor}} account access confirmation (use your configured credentials), the current employee/department roster with roles, and the target spend limits or budget bands I want per employee, department, or program (ask me for these numbers if I haven't given them).

Then, using {{vendor}}'s dashboard or API:
1. Review current card limits, roles, and permissions for each employee, department, and location.
2. Draft a proposed limit configuration: per-card spend limits for each employee, department/program-level budgets with enforced spend caps, and any granular role/permission changes needed (e.g., who can approve, view, or modify limits).
3. Flag any employees or departments with no current limit set, or limits that look inconsistent with peers in the same role/department.
4. Prepare a clear summary table: employee/department, current limit, proposed limit, rationale, and any role/permission changes.

Do NOT apply, save, or submit any limit or permission changes in {{vendor}} — only prepare drafts and pre-filled values in the dashboard or via API where possible without finalizing them. Once your draft configuration and summary table are ready, present them to me for review and stop for human sign-off before any changes are applied.

Report back with: the full proposed limit/permission table, any flagged inconsistencies or missing data, and a short list of open questions (e.g., ambiguous department assignments) that need my input before I approve and you finalize the changes.

scale_004:n3.prompt:
You are helping me set up expense approval workflows in {{vendor}}, our startup-banking platform. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our {{vendor}} account login context (assume I use my configured credentials), our org chart or list of departments/teams, spending thresholds we want enforced per department or program, and the names/emails of teammates who should hold approval permissions.

Once you have this information, do the following inside {{vendor}}:
1. Draft a set of expense rules that route bills and expenses through an approval workflow before any vendor payment is sent.
2. Draft department or program budget limits with automatically enforced spend caps, based on the thresholds I give you.
3. Prepare approval permission assignments so the designated teammates can approve and send payments with one click, matching the roles I specify.
4. Draft granular user roles and permissions across team members, locations, and departments as applicable to our org structure.

For each of these, prepare the configuration as a clear draft (rule names, thresholds, approver assignments, role mappings) inside {{vendor}}'s interface or save them as a summary document if the platform requires manual entry — do not activate or submit anything live yet.

When everything is prepared, compile a summary showing: the expense rules drafted, budget limits per department, approver assignments, and role/permission mappings. Flag any gaps where you lacked information to complete a rule.

This step requires a human to explicitly approve before changes are applied, so once your draft is ready, present it to me and stop for human sign-off. Do not activate workflows, enable rules, or grant permissions without my explicit approval.

scale_004:n4.prompt:
You are helping me configure {{vendor}} notifications for our expense management process so the finance team gets timely, non-noisy alerts about expense submissions, approvals, and reimbursements. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/domain, (2) the channel(s) that should receive expense notifications, and (3) any keywords or approval thresholds that should trigger extra alerts (e.g., 'urgent', amounts over a limit).

Using my configured credentials, please:
1. Create or locate an incoming webhook in {{vendor}} for the designated expense-notifications channel. If the provider's webhook API follows the pattern POST /webhooks/{webhook.id}/{webhook.token}, use that exact call to post a test expense notification message confirming the integration works.
2. Configure per-channel notification settings in {{vendor}} so routine messages are muted by default but keyword/mention alerts (e.g., 'expense approval needed', 'reimbursement overdue') trigger immediate notifications for admins.
3. Set up a notification schedule (e.g., quiet hours, digest vs. real-time) matching normal business hours unless I specify otherwise.
4. Document the webhook URL's location (without exposing the secret token in plain text) and the notification rules configured, in a short internal note.

Done looks like: a working webhook posting test messages into the correct channel, notification/keyword/schedule settings tuned per my instructions, and a summary I can review.

Report back with: the channel name configured, confirmation the test webhook message was received, a summary of notification rules set (keywords, schedule, mute settings), and any values you need me to confirm or adjust.

scale_004:n5.prompt:
You are helping me finalize and share our company's Expense Management policy document. Please ask me for any missing inputs: company name, expense categories and spending limits, approval workflow (who approves what thresholds), corporate card rules, reimbursement timelines/methods, and the audience/distribution channels I want to use (e.g., company email list, Slack channel, Google Drive/Notion/Confluence workspace).

Once you have this information, draft a clear, well-organized Expense Management Policy document covering: (1) purpose and scope, (2) expense reporting process and required documentation, (3) approval workflow with roles and thresholds, (4) corporate card usage rules and restrictions, and (5) reimbursement rules including timelines and payment methods. Use plain, unambiguous language suitable for all employees.

Also prepare a distribution plan: a short announcement message (for email or Slack) introducing the policy, a suggested storage location (e.g., shared drive folder or intranet page), and a list of who should receive or have access to it.

Present me with: (a) the full draft policy document, (b) the draft announcement message, and (c) the proposed distribution plan (recipients/channels and storage location). Do not publish, send, or share anything yet — do not post to Slack, send emails, or upload files. This requires my explicit approval before anything goes out, so stop for human sign-off once you have the drafts ready. Report back with the complete drafts and plan clearly labeled, awaiting my review and approval before any action is taken.
